source: Connecticut State Department of Education, EdSight; https://public-edsight.ct.gov/performance/connecticut-school-day-sat
notes: Connecticut SAT School Day, grade 11, ELA, 2021-22, all districts by race/ethnicity. Carries district-by-race rows: 734 data rows over 149 districts, of which 129 have a Black or African American row, 143 a Hispanic/Latino of any race row and 142 a White row. Layout: two title lines ('CT School Day SAT, <years>' and 'All Districts, <subject>, Race/Ethnicity'), a blank line, a spanner line, then the column header on line 5. Columns: District, District Code (CT state 7-digit code, written ='NNNNNNN', not an NCES LEAID), Race/Ethnicity, Total Number of Students, Total Number Tested, CT School Day SAT Participation Rate, Total Number with Scored Tests, then Count/% pairs for Level 1 Not Met, Level 2 Approaching, Level 3 Met, Level 4 Exceeded and Level 3&4 Met or Exceeded, then Average Score. District and District Code are printed once per district and blank on its later race rows. Race values: American Indian or Alaska Native, Asian, Black or African American, Hispanic/Latino of any race, Native Hawaiian or Other Pacific Islander, Two or More Races, White. Proficient = Level 3&4 (Met or Exceeded). '*' marks a suppressed cell, 'N/A' a cell with no base; no banded values are printed. Suppression rules: https://edsight.ct.gov/relatedreports/BDCRE%20Data%20Suppression%20Rules.pdf Matching rule (extension design Section 4): Run 1's EDFacts high school result for CT is the Connecticut SAT School Day, grade 11, Mathematics and Evidence-Based Reading and Writing (data/reference/test_replacement.csv, CT 2016-2021), so this report is the matching measure; ELA is the reading-and-writing subject and Math the mathematics subject. The report has no grade control (the CT SAT School Day is grade 11 only) and no regular/alternate test-group control, so the 'regular plus alternate where the tool pools them' clause does not bite: the report is the SAT School Day alone and the Connecticut Alternate Assessment is reported elsewhere on EdSight. Proficiency is the state's federal-accountability definition for the year. Section 9 codes CT 2024 (digital SAT on the College Board's linked scale) as 0, not a replacement. Export from the EdSight interactive report; no posted file, so url is blank. Steps as run 2026-09-16: open https://public-edsight.ct.gov/performance/connecticut-school-day-sat, which frames the SAS stored process /CTDOE/EdSight/Release/Reporting/Public/Reports/StoredProcesses/CTSchoolDaySATReport_SiteCore on edsight.ct.gov; set Year=2021-22, District='All Districts', Schools=(blank), Subject=ELA, Filter By='Race/Ethnicity' (the select value is 'Race '), Submit; then follow the report's 'Export .csv file' link, which is the same stored-process path with _program=.../StoredProcesses/CTSchoolDaySATExport and the same _year, _district, _subject and _subgroup=Race. The report form can be reached directly at https://edsight.ct.gov/SASStoredProcess/guest?_year=2021-22&_district=All+Districts&_school=&_subject=ELA&_subgroup=Race+&_program=%2FCTDOE%2FEdSight%2FRelease%2FReporting%2FPublic%2FReports%2FStoredProcesses%2FCTSchoolDaySATReport_SiteCore&_select=Submit and the export at https://edsight.ct.gov/SASStoredProcess/do?_program=%2FCTDOE%2FEdSight%2FRelease%2FReporting%2FPublic%2FReports%2FStoredProcesses%2FCTSchoolDaySATExport&_year=2021-22&_district=All+Districts&_subgroup=Race&_school=+&_subject=ELA; the export always lands as CTSchoolDaySAT.csv and was renamed on arrival. Chrome blocked the in-page Export link as a repeated automatic download on some passes; navigating the tab to the export url downloaded it every time.

notes: Export driven in the browser 2026-09-15. Steps: open https://www.idahoreportcard.org/datafiles; the welcome modal asks for a role (Researcher or Advocate) and 'Enter the Idaho State Report Card'; click 'Achievement - ISAT ELA Proficiency' or 'Achievement - ISAT Math Proficiency'; in the Quick Data Download modal click 'Customize Download'; (1) Select Districts = All Districts; (2) Select Measures = the one ISAT subject; (3) Select School Year(s) = 2021-2022 only, unticking the default 2025-2026; (4) Select Student Group Breakdowns = Black, Hispanic and White under Ethnicity/Race (All Students is always included; Grade Levels offers Grade 3-12 and High School); (5) File Type = CSV, Data Layout = Long Format; 'Download Data File' starts a five-second countdown and writes IdahoReportCard_DataExport_Normalized_<UTC stamp>.csv to the browser download folder. Columns: Organization ID, Organization Name, Organization Type (State/District/School), District ID, District Name, Measure Label, Student Group, School Year, Rate, Text Value, Student Count, NSize, Suppression Type. NOT ARCHIVED, no checksum. The export carries district-by-race rows, but not for the measure the design's matching rule names. 'Student Group' is a single dimension: the race groups pool every tested grade (ISAT is given in grades 3-8 and 11; statewide ELA NSize 166,133 in 2021-22) and 'High School' is a separate group pooling every race (NSize 22,848). Selecting Grade 11 returns no rows at all; selecting High School together with Black/White returns them as three separate groups, never crossed. The district Student Breakdown page is built the same way, with 'Race, Ethnicity and Gender' and 'Grades Served' as separate tables. Run 1 reported Idaho's high school ISAT (test_replacement.csv: ISAT by Smarter Balanced, high school grade = grade 11), so extension Section 4's matching rule cannot be met from this source. Alternative not taken, author decision needed: the legacy SDE workbook, no longer live but archived, does cross grade and race at district level. Wayback replay https://web.archive.org/web/20221108225742id_/https://sde.idaho.gov/assessment/accountability/files/accountability-results/2022/2022-ISAT-Results.xlsx (capture 2022-11-08, sha256 47bfccd758be62f93ac857123cdafc37120a64adabde9f6f7223315cc565811f, 8,943,310 bytes). Sheet 'Districts', columns District Id, DistrictName, Subject Name, Grade (All Grades, Grade 3-8, High School), Population (including Black / African American, Hispanic or Latino, White): 1,293 High School by those three groups rows over 144 districts in ELA, Math and Science. CAUTION: this year carries rates only (Advanced/Proficient/Basic/Below Basic Rate) and no tested count, which Run 1 rule 3 requires. source: Michigan Department of Education / CEPI (MI School Data); https://www.mischooldata.org/k-12-data-files/
notes: DELIVERED AND ARCHIVED 2026-09-16, BUT IT DOES NOT CARRY THE ROWS THE MATCHING RULE NAMES - AUTHOR DECISION NEEDED. The 2021-22 request described below was delivered and the file is in place as data/raw/hs_reportcards/MI/hs_MI_2022_all.csv (31,512,491 bytes); it was checksummed on 2026-09-16 and downloaded_utc is the file's own time, 2026-09-16T04:55:45Z. Layout: plain CSV, CRLF line endings, one header row, 46 columns, 73,540 data rows, every row GradeContentTested 11 and SchoolYear '21 - 22 School Year'. Columns: SchoolYear, TestType, TestPopulation, ISDCode, ISDName, DistrictCode, DistrictName, BuildingCode, BuildingName, CountyCode, CountyName, EntityType, SchoolLevel, Locale, MISTEM_NAME, MISTEM_CODE, GradeContentTested, Subject, ReportCategory, then Total/Percent counts by performance level, NumberAssessed and the scale-score columns. A district total row is BuildingCode '00000' with DistrictCode not '00000'; the state row is DistrictCode '00000'. ReportCategory is the subgroup dimension and carries the study's three groups as 'Black or African American', 'Hispanic of Any Race' and 'White'. Suppressed counts print as '<10'. It carries district-by-race rows - 29,067 district total rows over 690 districts - but NOT for the assessment the matching rule names. TestType takes two values only, M-STEP and MI-Access, and there are no SAT rows in the file at all (the only occurrence of the string SAT anywhere in it is the district name Satterlee School). TestType by Subject: M-STEP carries Science (20,999 rows) and Social Studies (20,990) alone; ELA (8,915) and Mathematics (8,819) appear under MI-Access only, whose TestPopulation values are FI, P and SI - the alternate assessment for students with significant cognitive disabilities. The grade-11 ELA and mathematics district-by-race rows therefore number 1,483 over 373 districts but are alternate-only: Black or African American 165 (ELA) and 161 (math), Hispanic of Any Race 109 and 107, White 472 and 469, with a median NumberAssessed of 12 and a maximum of 64, against a statewide MI-Access FI ELA total of 1,038 students. Run 1's EDFacts high school result for Michigan is grade 11 SAT Mathematics and SAT Evidence-Based Reading and Writing, and EDFacts pools regular with alternate; this file is the alternate side alone, with no regular assessment to pool it with, so extension design Section 4's matching rule cannot be met from it. Whether to request a different MI School Data file (the page also offers 'SAT Math Proficiency Cross-tabulated Data', 'SAT EBRW Proficiency Cross-tabulated Data' and 'College Readiness (Includes SAT Data)', none of which was requested and none of which is known to carry district-by-race rows in the form the design needs) is an author decision, and it is open for 2022 and for the three years still undelivered. The file stays archived as the record of the check. THE RECORD OF THE REQUEST, WRITTEN BEFORE THE FILE ARRIVED: the request was submitted in the browser on 2026-09-16 and no file has been received, so url, filename, sha256 and downloaded_utc are blank. The MI School Data K-12 Data Files page builds the file on the server and delivers it to an email address rather than serving a static url, which is why the manifest row is hand_download with a blank url. Steps, as driven 2026-09-16: open https://www.mischooldata.org/k-12-data-files/; leave the three Select Locations dropdowns at their statewide defaults (ISD 'All ISDs in State', Districts 'All Districts in State', School 'All Schools in State'), which is the selection that yields district rows; type the delivery address dylanscully01123@gmail.com into the Email box; set School Year to '2021-22'; leave Report Category at 'Assessment and Accountability'; under Data Files tick 'High School Assessments' alone, leaving every other box clear - it is the district-level high school results file whose ReportCategory field carries the Race/Ethnicity groups, whereas the 'SAT Math Proficiency Cross-tabulated Data' and 'SAT EBRW Proficiency Cross-tabulated Data' files are subgroup-by-subgroup cross-tabulations and 'College Readiness (Includes SAT Data)' is the college-benchmark file; then click the button below Data Files, which reads 'Settings Require Changes' until the form is complete and 'Send Results' once it is. The page then replaced the form with the settings summary 'Location(s) All ISDs in State All Districts in State All Schools in State / Report: 2021-22 Assessment and Accountability High School Assessments' and the message 'School Data File Created'. That message is the whole of the site's acknowledgement: it carries no request identifier, no turnaround time and no statement of how the file is sent, so delivery is expected at the address typed into the Email box and is unverified until it arrives. The four school years were requested one at a time, the settings panel being reopened with its 'Edit' control between submissions; the email address, the report category and the ticked data file carry over and only School Year changes. Matching rule (extension design Section 4): the request form offers no grade, test or test-group selector - one High School Assessments file is generated whole per school year - so the rule is applied when the delivered file is read, not at request time. Run 1's EDFacts high school result for Michigan is grade 11, SAT Mathematics and SAT Evidence-Based Reading and Writing within the Michigan Merit Exam (data/reference/test_replacement.csv, MI 2016-2021; docs/recon_run2_hs.csv hs_grade 11), so the rows to read are grade 11, test SAT, subjects Mathematics and Evidence-Based Reading and Writing, with the test group taken as regular plus alternate pooled wherever the file pools them, EDFacts pooling regular and alternate assessments; proficient = Proficient + Advanced on the MDE SAT performance levels. Nothing is recorded here about the file's format, layout, district-by-race row counts or suppression marks: none of it can be checked until the file arrives.

source: Nebraska Department of Education, Nebraska Education Profile (NEP); https://nep.education.ne.gov/#/data-downloads
notes: Export driven in the browser 2026-09-15. Steps: open https://nep.education.ne.gov/#/data-downloads; click the row 'Download File Description (2021-2022)' to expand it (the first click after page load is sometimes swallowed - click the row again); click 'ACT Assessments Data All Subjects'. That row issues GET https://nepdata.education.ne.gov/api/v1/data/downloads/data-file?dataYear=20212022&fileName=ACT_AllSubjects_20212022.csv, which returns 200 and writes ACT_AllSubjects_20212022.csv (4,779,331 bytes, sha256 d587133eec787e298cd360208a4f4d93cafbb3e855b77c500e71411179aeced9) to the browser download folder. CORRECTION to the earlier NE manifest note: a plain GET on that URL does work and needs no session, cookie or referer - dataYear must be the eight-digit school year (20212022), not the end year. The file list behind the page is GET https://nepdata.education.ne.gov/api/v1/data/downloads, which gives displayName and fileName for every year. ARCHIVED FILE: the download filtered to the rows with Datayears = 20212022, Level = DI (district) and Subject = 'MATHEMATICS'. The header line and every column are kept byte for byte (UTF-8 BOM, CRLF line endings); no value was altered and nothing was added. The download itself is one file per release covering all subjects, so it cannot be archived under the one-file-per-state-year-subject name; it is reproducible from the URL and checksum above. MATCHING RULE (extension design Section 4). Run 1's EDFacts high school result for NE is the ACT at grade 11 (data/reference/test_replacement.csv: 'ACT Mathematics grade 11' and 'ACT Reading grade 11', flagged as a replacement in 2017 when the ACT replaced the NeSA at grade 11). Test = the NEP ACT file. Grade = 11: Nebraska administers the ACT to grade 11 only and the file carries no other grade (the 2023-24 and 2024-25 layouts have a Grade column whose only value is ALL). Subject = the file's ENGLISH LANGUAGE ARTS for the reading/language arts gap and MATHEMATICS for the mathematics gap; SCIENCE is not used. Proficiency definition = the state's federal accountability levels published in this file (see the level columns below). TEST GROUP = regular only. NEP does not pool the alternate assessment into the ACT file: the grade 11 alternate sits in the separate NSCAS files (NSCAS_ELA_Proficient_<year>.csv, NSCAS_Math_Proficient_<year>.csv), which do carry Grade = 11 rows for a few hundred students statewide - this corrects the earlier NE manifest note, which said the NSCAS files cover grades 3-8 only. Section 4's pooling clause therefore does not bite (the tool does not pool them), but EDFacts did pool regular and alternate, so this export is regular-only where Run 1 was pooled. LAYOUT (2021-22 and 2022-23 releases, 19 columns): Level, Datayears, COUNTY, DISTRICT, SCHOOL, NAME, SUBJECT, SUBGROUP_TYPE, SUBGROUP_DESCRIPTION, AVERAGE_SCALE_SCORE, DEVELOPING_COUNT, DEVELOPING_PERCENT, ON_TRACK_COUNT, ON_TRACK_PERCENT, ACT_BENCHMARK_COUNT, ACT_BENCHMARK_PERCENT, TESTED_COUNT, NOT_TESTED, NOT_TESTED_PERCENT. notes: Nevada Report Card Data Interaction, Group Summary Report, exam 'CCR (Grade 11 High School ELA/Math)', all 20 districts plus the State row, disaggregated by Race/Ethnicity, Mathematics data fields only. Carries district-by-race rows: 138 data rows over 21 organizations (State plus the 20 districts the tool lists), 117 of them race rows; of the 20 districts 15 have a Black row, 20 a Hispanic row and 20 a White row. Layout: title line 1 'Group Summary Report', line 2 'CCR (Grade 11 High School ELA/Math), Year 2021-2022', a blank line, then the column header on line 4. Twelve columns: Organization Code, Group, Year, '# of students enrolled during testing window', then five Mathematics fields written 'Mathematics - <field>': Number Tested, % Not Tested, % Tested, % Proficient, and the four performance-level shares % Emergent/Developing, % Approaches Standard, % Meets Standard, % Exceeds Standard. An organization's own row carries the district name in Group; its race rows follow with the race in Group and the same Organization Code. Organization Code is a positional index 00-20 within the selection, not an NCES LEAID, and Group names the district, so the loader matches on name. The 20 districts are the 17 county districts plus Carson City, and three non-regular entities (State Charters, University, Correctional) that Run 1 rule 1 removes. Race values: American Indian / Alaskan Native, Black, Hispanic, White, Two or More Races, Asian, Pacific Islander; a race with no students in a district has no row. Proficient = Meets Standard + Exceeds Standard (checked against the printed shares). Symbols, from the tool's footnotes (https://nevadareportcard.nv.gov/DIWAPI-NVReportCard/api/Footnote, scope e25): '-' is data not presented for groups fewer than 10 under FERPA, '--' is a group of more than 10 suppressed under FERPA; percentages at the extremes are printed as bounds '<5' and '>95'; no banded ranges are printed. A further footnote: 'District totals do not include state or district sponsored charter school data. (2008- Current)'. The download covers both pages of the paged table, all 21 organizations. The resulting report state is in the page URL as /di/report/summary_1 with report=summary_1, scope=e25.y19 (e25 = the CCR exam, y19/y20/y21/y22 = 2021-22/2022-23/2023-24/2024-25), organization=<selection id>, scores=N_MA,MA_NotTested,MA_Tested,MA_Pass,MA_level, subgroups=ethnicity, pagesize=20; the organization id is created by the selection step and is not a stable public identifier, so the selection is redone rather than reused. source: North Dakota Department of Public Instruction / ITD, Insights; https://insights.nd.gov/Data
notes: Export driven in the browser 2026-09-16. The static 'View' url https://insights.nd.gov/ShowFile?f=10006_6_csv_2024-2025 still returns the empty 153-byte HTML shell in csv, json and excel form alike; every other Insights dataset's 2024-2025 View url returns the same shell, so the failure is the year's View links, not this dataset. The page's own 'Download' control was attempted for the first time and it works. Steps: open https://insights.nd.gov/Data; expand 'Assessment Performance' with the + toggle at the left of its heading (the page function is ToggleHidden(10006)); in the 'Assessment Performance - 2024-2025' row click 'Download' in the CSV File column - it is an ASP.NET __doPostBack (ctl00$ContentPlaceHolderNoSideNav$rptGroups$ctl04$rptFiles$ctl10$rptYearFiles$ctl00$lnkFile) with no static url, so the url field is blank; Chrome saves Insights-AssessmentPerformance-CSV-2024-2025-v20251113.csv, which is renamed to the archived name. Unlike the 2022-2024 View files the Download body is plain CSV with no HTML wrapper; the columns are unchanged (AcademicYear, InstitutionName, InstitutionID, Grade, Subject, AssessmentType, Accomodations, Subgroup, then the Novice/Partially/Proficient/Advanced RangeLow and RangeHigh pairs). One export covers the whole dataset: the Data page offers no grade, subject or assessment-type selector, so the file is archived whole (_all) and the extension design Section 4 matching rule is applied when it is read. Matching rule for North Dakota: Run 1's EDFacts high school result is the grade 10 state assessment (data/reference/test_replacement.csv, ND 2018-2021; docs/recon_run2_hs.csv hs_grade 10), which in 2024-25 is the ND A+ Summative that replaced the NDSA, so the rows to read are Grade='10', AssessmentType='Comp' - the file's pooled regular-plus-alternate figure, the alternatives being 'Reg' and 'Alt' - and Subject 'Math' and 'Reading'. Carries district-by-race rows: 66,438 data rows, of which 24,616 are 5-digit InstitutionID district rows over 160 districts (10-digit ids are schools). At Grade 10 / Comp there are 447 Math and 445 Reading district rows over 117 districts; in both subjects a Black row is present for 8 districts, a Hispanic row for 10 and a White row for 18, each with a printed proficiency range. Grade 11 rows, present in 2022-2024 from the locally selected ACT option, are absent in 2024-2025. Proficiency is published as low-high ranges rather than point values, as in the earlier years. Downloading from this page accepts the SLDS De-Identified Information Data Use Agreement printed on it (statistical use only, no attempt to re-identify, no linking to other data); the file is public and is deposited with the manifest.

notes: 2021-2022: 21,187 data rows. Carries district-by-race rows: 444 grade-11 Regular-and-Alternate district rows over 148 districts (148 per subject). Of the 148 district rows a printed proficiency percentage appears for Black/African American in 2 (ELA) and 2 (math), Hispanic/Latino in 9 and 8, White/Caucasian in 122 and 119; the rest are '*'. Grade values present: 03-08, 11, 12, All. Project SD_ARC_PUBLIC_2122, valuePromptAnswers 99999^2021 (academic year 2021-2022). South Dakota Report Card DATA DOWNLOAD (MicroStrategy), report 'State Assessment Results: All Students', exported whole for the school year named. Matching rule (extension design Section 4): Run 1's EDFacts high school result for SD is the Smarter Balanced grade 11 assessment in mathematics and English language arts (data/reference/test_replacement.csv, SD 2015-2021), and Section 4 fixes South Dakota's test group as regular plus alternate, so the matching rows are Grade Levels = '11' and Test Taken = 'Regular and Alternate'; proficiency is the state's federal-accountability definition, Level 3 or Level 4. IMPORTANT: the EXPORT link does not honour the document's GRADE LEVELS and SUBGROUP selectors. They were set to 11 and (All) as the recorded steps say, but EXPORT runs the panel's underlying report (reportID A2995CDB40EA419DFAA6A9993F4D7C93, the same GUID in every year's project) with the academic-year prompt alone, so the archived file is the whole report: every grade, all three subjects, all three Test Taken groups, and state, district and school rows. The grade, subject, test-group and level filtering is left to the loader. Layout: UTF-16LE with a BOM, comma separated, LF line endings, 334 columns, two header rows and then the data. Header row 1 names the subgroup over each 19-column metric block; header row 2 names the metric but always prefixes it 'All Students - ' whatever the subgroup, so the subgroup must be read from row 1, not row 2. Columns 1-10 are Academic Year; District name; District code (the 5-digit SD district code, e.g. 06001, NOT an NCES LEAID); District name repeated; School name; School number; Grade Levels; Subject; Test Taken; Accommodations. Column 11 is an empty 'Metrics' label column. Columns 12-334 are 17 subgroups x 19 metrics: All Levels - N-Size; Tested - Number of Students; Tested - Percentage; Level 1 to Level 4 Number of Students and Percentage; Level 3 or Level 4 - Number of Students and Percentage; Not Tested; Not Scoreable; Medically Exempt (number and percentage each). District total rows are School = 'All Schools' with School number '00'; the state row is District = 'All Districts', code 00000. Subgroup labels for the study's three groups are 'Black/African American', 'Hispanic/Latino' and 'White/Caucasian'. Proficiency = 'Level 3 or Level 4 - Percentage'; participation = 'Tested - Percentage'; the tested count is 'Tested - Number of Students'. Suppression: '*' is the only non-numeric token in the race cells (the footer reads that data are not shown to prevent student identification or are not available); no banded or range values are printed, so the design's range-midpoint rule does not bite for South Dakota. Export settings as run: report selector 'State Assessment Results: All Students'; Export = 'Whole report'; format 'CSV file format'; 'Export Report Title' UNCHECKED (so the file starts at the column headers); 'Export filter details' unchecked; 'Remove extra column' = Automatic. Steps as run 2026-09-16: open the DATA DOWNLOAD document at https://sdschoolreportcard.sd.gov/MicroStrategy/servlet/mstrWeb?evt=2048001&src=mstrWeb.2048001&documentID=919F9ED9428AF91F8B9613869168454C&currentViewMedia=1&visMode=0&Server=ESPR10445&Project=<project>&Port=0&ru=1&share=1&ConnMode=8&hiddenSections=header,footer,path,dockTop,dockLeft,dockBottom&valuePromptAnswers=99999%5E<promptyear> (project names and URL template from https://sdschools.sd.gov/assets/config/config.json); in the unlabeled report selector choose 'State Assessment Results: All Students'; set GRADE LEVELS to 11 and SUBGROUP to (All); then EXPORT. The EXPORT button posts a form into a window opened with window.open, which Chrome's popup blocker kills (console: TypeError: Cannot set properties of null (setting 'opener') in mstrmojo.form.safeSubmitForm), and no export is produced. Workaround used instead of changing any browser setting: read the EXPORT text field's own link, which is ./mstrWeb?evt=3067&src=mstrWeb.3067&executionMode=4&showOptionsPage=true&reportID=A2995CDB40EA419DFAA6A9993F4D7C93&valuePromptAnswers=99999%5E<promptyear>, and open it directly (adding &Server=ESPR10445&Project=<project>&Port=0 so the right year's project is used). That is the Export Options page; set the format and the title checkbox there and press Export. The file always arrives named 'State Assessment Results_ All Students - Export.csv' and was renamed on arrival. The export is deterministic: re-running the 2023-24 export in the same session returned a byte-identical file (same sha256). File naming: SD's export has no subject control and one export carries English Language Arts, Mathematics and Science, so the file is named hs_SD_<sy_end>_all.csv rather than one file per subject.

source: Texas Education Agency, Texas Academic Performance Report (TAPR); https://rptsvr1.tea.texas.gov/perfreport/tapr/2022/download/DownloadData.html
notes: Texas Academic Performance Report (TAPR), district-level STAAR EOC Algebra I results by race/ethnicity, school year 2021-22. Matching rule (extension design Section 4): Run 1's EDFacts high school result for Texas is the STAAR end-of-course tests, Algebra I for mathematics and English II for reading/language arts (data/reference/test_replacement.csv, TX 2014-2021), so the math file carries the EOC Algebra I columns and the ela file the EOC English II columns; grade is not a selection, an end-of-course test has none. Test group: TAPR publishes one EOC performance table with no regular/alternate split, and the TAPR glossary (Performance, Other Important Information) records that the TAPR and the TPRS include STAAR with and without accommodations together with STAAR Alternate 2, so the figure the tool gives is already the pooled one Section 4 calls for. Performance levels are reported separately as Approaches, Meets and Masters Grade Level; Texas's federal accountability academic achievement definition is Meets Grade Level, and all three levels are kept so the loader can apply it. Export steps (browser, 2026-09-16): TAPR 2021-22 Download Options (https://rptsvr1.tea.texas.gov/perfreport/tapr/2022/download.html) then 'Advanced TAPR Data (Numerators, Denominators & Rates)' at https://rptsvr1.tea.texas.gov/perfreport/tapr/2022/download/DownloadData.html; question 1 What type of data = District (sumlev=D); question 2 category = STAAR Assessment Data: Primary Student Groups, 'Approaches, Meets, and Masters Grade Level (EOC, SAT/ACT Accelerated Testers, All Grades)' (setpick=STAAR2); Continue. The form POSTs to https://rptsvr1.tea.texas.gov/cgi/sas/broker (a SAS broker, so there is no file URL) and the browser saves DISTSTAAR2.csv. The broker answers HTTP 503 intermittently; resubmitting the same form succeeds. Saved file: the export cut down to DISTRICT, DISTNAME and every column of the named test, in the export's own column order, with header text stripped of the line breaks the SAS export wraps into its long header line; no value is altered and no row is dropped. The other EOC tests (English I, Biology, US History) and the SAT/ACT accelerated-tester columns are not kept, and the full export is not archived. Layout: one header row of TAPR variable codes, then 1207 district rows; DISTRICT is column 1 and DISTNAME column 128. DISTRICT is the TEA 6-digit county-district number (written with a leading apostrophe in the 2022 and 2023 exports, plain in 2024 and 2025), not an NCES LEAID, so a crosswalk is needed before the sample rules can be applied. A variable code reads [D level][D domain or N new][student group][00A][test][performance level][2-digit year][N numerator, D denominator or R rate], so every kept column has 00AA11 in character positions 4 to 9. Student groups: 18 in this export, among them All Students, African American, Hispanic, White, American Indian, Asian, Pacific Islander and Two or More Races. Each group has seven columns: the denominator (number of tests, performance-level character 0, suffix D), the Approaches, Meets and Masters numerators (performance-level characters S, 2, 3, suffix N) and the three matching rates (suffix R). Missing-value codes: -1 and -3 mark masked cells and '.' a cell with no base; no banded or range values are printed. Carries district-by-race rows: of 1207 district rows, 1113 have an All Students test count, 409 an African American count, 847 a Hispanic count and 882 a White count; 389 districts have both an African American and a White count and 726 have both a Hispanic and a White count. These are counts of districts with an unmasked denominator; no performance figure was inspected. Caveats for the harmonization table: (1) the TAPR STAAR Performance section reports the state accountability subset, students enrolled in the same district on both the October PEIMS snapshot date and the test date, which is narrower than the EDFacts all-testers count; (2) the header conventions differ across the four years (codes only in 2022 and 2023, 'District <year> Domain 1A: <level>, <group>, <test> <metric>' labels in 2024, 'STAAR Performance, <test>, SY <years>, <group>, <metric>' labels in 2025) while the underlying variable codes are the same in all four; (3) the number of student groups grows from 18 in the 2022 and 2023 Primary Student Groups export to 26 in 2024 and 27 in 2025, but the three groups the gaps need are in all four; (4) TAPR reports no participation rate in this table, so under extension design Section 5 the participation rule is recorded as not applicable unless it is taken from the separate STAAR Participation table; (5) the 2022-23 STAAR redesign is already coded as a test replacement for TX 2023 in extension design Section 9. Explanation of masking: https://rptsvr1.tea.texas.gov/perfreport/tapr/2022/masking.html TAPR glossary: https://rptsvr1.tea.texas.gov/perfreport/tapr/2022/glossary.pdf

notes: Export driven in the browser 2026-09-16. The report is built on request, has no fixed file URL, and the CSV downloads 2-5 minutes later as AssessmentPerformanceResultsDistrictNew_<UTC timestamp>.csv, renamed here. Trap: the lists cascade. Changing School Year or Subjects queues a reset of the Grade and Subgroup lists which is applied when RUN REPORT is pressed, even though the boxes still show the old ticks, so Grade and Subgroup must be re-selected after every School Year or Subjects change or the report runs for all grades and all subgroups. Matching rule (extension design Section 4): Run 1's EDFacts high school result for WY is WY-TOPP grade 10, Mathematics and English language arts (data/reference/test_replacement.csv, end years 2018-2021, unchanged since the 2017-18 replacement of the ACT), so grade 10 is taken and grade 09 is not, against the grade 09 and 10 in the earlier reconnaissance note. Test group: the report is the pooled 'Grades 3-10 WY-TOPP/WY-ALT Performance Results' report and offers no test-group parameter, so regular and alternate are pooled as EDFacts pools them; the Subgroup list's 'Students with Disabilities by Test Type' entries are a separate breakdown and are not used. Carries district-by-race rows: 192 data rows, four per district over 48 districts (All Students, Race / Ethnicity: Black, Race / Ethnicity: Hispanic, Race / Ethnicity: White), one school year, one subject, grade 10; every district carries all three race rows. Layout: one header line, then one row per district-subgroup, no title or footer lines; UTF-8 with a byte order mark. Columns: School Year, District Name, Subgroup, Specific Grade, Subject, No. of Students Tested, Participation Rate, Percent Below Basic, Percent Basic, Percent Proficient, Percent Advanced, Percent Basic & Below, Percent Proficient & Advanced; the header cells carry literal commas inside their quotes ('School,Year', 'No. of,Students,Tested'). Proficient = Percent Proficient & Advanced. District Name is the WDE district name (e.g. 'Albany #1'), not an NCES LEAID, so the loader must map names to LEAIDs. Suppression: the tested count is always printed as a band, of width 4, 5 or 10 (e.g. '290 - 299'), and the only exact value printed is 0, so Run 1 rule 3's exact tested count is not available for this state; percentages are printed exactly, as an open-ended inequality ('<= 5%', '<= 10%', '<= 20%', '>= 80%', '>= 90%'), or left blank, and Participation Rate is blank wherever the group is suppressed. 66 of the 144 race rows carry a proficiency figure.
